notes: Both coders found the one CTE page (three Academic Affairs-approved sample syllabus statements) and both set stance to delegates with three tiers. Main disagreements: (1) policy_type: P72 vs UNCOVERED for 'supplementary tool rather than a replacement for human interaction' (UNCOVERED, nobody is directed to human help); P77 vs P36 for 'completed per the University's Administrative Guidelines on Academic Integrity' (P77, no misconduct classification); P01 vs P06 for 'You may not engage in unauthorized collaboration or use ChatGPT' (P01, an explicit ban, not a silent-syllabus fallback). (2) actor for the 'three sample statements' unit, admin vs instructor (instructor, the page addresses faculty). (3) phase for the Academic Integrity Guidelines clause, general vs during-work (during-work). (4) unit_stance on three units (both fact-checking duties and 'work must be your own'), A permit/restrict/prohibit vs B neutral, resolved to neutral because the sentences do not themselves take a position on AI use; this does not enter the shares above. (5) Anchor, policy-wording and topic differences were harmonized; B's 'if any' in the instructor-choice policy was dropped as unsupported. The only-A unit ('Intellectual honesty is vital to an academic community...') is a real rationale statement and was kept, recoded from P56 to UNCOVERED. Final file has 20 units; no new_types.
